problem: Zero-shot ObjectNav methods with VLMs abstract the environment into semantic/value maps, text or scene graphs, so high-level decisions are bottlenecked by low-level perception accuracy and lose continuous spatial structure.
motivation: VLMs have strong spatial and planning reasoning, but scene abstractions prevent them from using it. Providing renderable, persistent visual memory could let the VLM reason directly over images of frontiers, and novel-view rendering can also verify detections without physically moving.
key_idea: Build an online 3D Gaussian Splatting map via active perception as persistent VLM memory, render optimized first-person views of frontiers plus an annotated BEV as structured visual prompts with CoT for frontier selection, and re-verify detections via VLM-chosen virtual viewpoints in the 3DGS.
insight: Rendered free viewpoints avoid wall occlusion of frontiers: removing virtual viewpoints drops SPL from 51.79 to 38.54 on HM3Dv1. Re-verification (SR 53.75 without the VLM verifier vs 80.0) and frontier clustering (62.5 without) matter greatly. A stronger planner VLM (Gemini3 vs Qwen3-VL-235B) gives clear gains, and reasoning failures are only 9.5% of failures, with detection and simulator category ambiguity dominating.
method: Active perception: renders a panoramic opacity field from the 3DGS, clusters low-opacity regions with DBSCAN, and drives the real camera/manipulator to the largest missing region (pitch/yaw) instead of passive rotation scanning.

Exploration map and frontier clustering: top-down opacity rendering after removing floor and ceiling Gaussians gives the map. Frontiers are extracted following L3MVN, refined by Chebyshev distance, and clustered by a distance-field skeleton with watershed segmentation, taking region centroids.
Guidance trajectory: Dijkstra with a distance-transform cost and an exponential obstacle-proximity penalty gives a path to each frontier.

Virtual viewpoint init + free-viewpoint optimization: the initial position on the path maximizes a curvature/distance score within [r_min, r_max]. Camera pose (quaternion and translation) is then optimized for 40 iterations with opacity, ray-occlusion, view-alignment and guidance-trajectory losses.

Structured visual annotation and CoT planning: the FPV gets a gaze point and purple unobserved regions. The BEV shows frontiers, guidance trajectory, history (blue) and current pose (purple triangle). The composite image plus CoT prompt goes to Gemini3-Pro to choose a frontier, and FMM navigates to it.

Re-verification: YOLOE open-vocabulary detector flags targets, and GLM-4.5v picks virtual actions (forward/backward 0.25 m, turn 10°, leave; max 5 per cycle) executed in the 3DGS to render new views for confirming targets.

setting.backbone: Gemini3-Pro (planner, frozen) + GLM-4.5v (action/verification VLM, frozen) + YOLOE-11m-seg detector; 3DGS optimized online
setting.training_data: none (training-free, zero-shot; 3DGS optimized online per episode)
setting.action_space: Habitat discrete: forward 0.2 m, turn ±30°, look up/down 40°, stop; long-term frontier goals via FMM. Virtual verification actions rendered in 3DGS
setting.simulator: Habitat (HM3Dv1, HM3Dv2, MP3D) + real Go2 quadruped

numbers_note: Split names are not stated in the paper; 'val' is assumed. Ablation SR values like 77.96 and 53.75 suggest smaller evaluation subsets (e.g. 60-80 episodes), unconfirmed. Real-world results: 5/6, 4/6, 5/6, 4/6, 4/6, 3/6 (69.44% overall).
results: 3DGSNav beats ApexNav on HM3Dv1 (SR 80.0 vs 59.6, SPL 51.79 vs 33.0) and MP3D (43.63 vs 39.2). On HM3Dv2 SPL is higher (44.19 vs 38.0) but SR is lower (75.0 vs 76.2). It achieves 69.44% SR on a real Go2 quadruped.
limitations: No cross-floor navigation (2D policy); failures dominated by detection issues, category and multi-target ambiguity, and VLM conservative exploration/hallucination.
Dependence on strong proprietary VLMs (Gemini3-Pro) with API latency; open-source Qwen models perform notably worse.
Real-world issues: payload-induced instability, motion blur, RGB-D failures on glass/reflective surfaces, and small trial counts (6 per scenario).
